 J U D G M E N T
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 27.10.2022 at about 8.50 to 9.00 p.m., he was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KJ-8911 from Devegowda Main Road, on extreme left side of Dinnur Main Road and when he reached at Citizen Park Back Side Road, Bengaluru City, a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-JW-4744, ridden by its rider at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against his motor cycle.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was shifted to V-care Hospital, Devegowda Road and then referred to Ramaiah Medical College Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyances, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and working as Police Head Constable, Police Department, Government of Karnataka, Bengaluru and earning a sum of .57,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

3. The petition against respondent No.1 is dismissed as per order dated: 28.11.2024 and respondent No.2 is deleted as per order dated:
05.04.2024.
The respondent No.3 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.3 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.3 has also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.3 has contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that the motor cycle stood insured with them as on the date of accident vide policy No.3005/166879980/00/000 and valid from 13.03.2019 to 12.03.2024 and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions.

Further respondent No.3 has admitted the issuance of policy to the motor cycle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and Kumar A.R. Alias Kumarappa A.R vs Sujith Kumar Guptha on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162073866/

sentences.text: Further contended that the motor cycle was not at all involved in the accident and the rider of alleged vehicle was in no way related in alleged accident as on the date of accident.
Further, the alleged date of accident is 27.10.2022 but the claim petition is filed on 25.05.2023, after the lapse of six months from the date of accident.
Further the rider of motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Further the alleged accident was happened due to the negligence of petitioner and there is no negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 27.10.2022 at about 08.50 p.m., to 09.00 p.m., on Dinnur Main Road at Citizen Park Back side road, Bengaluru, when petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KJ-8911, due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-JW-4744 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got examined Dr.S.Ramachandra, working as Senior Consultant in Orthopaedic and DNB Post Graduates Professor at General Hospital, Jayanagar, Bengaluru as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.22 and closed evidence of his side.
On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.R.1 & 2 and closed evidence of their side.

7. Heard the arguments of both the side and perused the materials available on record.
8.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:-

9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner has contended that on 27.10.2022 at about 08.50 to 09.00 p.m.,
accident occurred on Dinnur Main Road at Citizen Park Back Side Road, Bengaluru, when he was riding Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KJ-8911, due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-JW-4744 by its rider in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to prove rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-JW-4744 by its rider, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 has deposed that due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross- examination of PW.1 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner.
11. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.2, first information statement.
On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, petitioner has lodged complaint with police on 19.11.2022 with respect to the accident occurred on 27.10.2022.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
The FIR is registered against the rider of offending vehicle which does not appear to have been questioned or challenged in any manner.
The petitioner also furnished Mahazar and sketch, which are marked as Ex.P.3 & 5.
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle and said aspect is disclosed in the sketch also.
The sketch depicts the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The rider of offending vehicle is stated to be approaching the main road from the cross road and he does not appear to be approaching the main in the proper course.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the facts, as shown in the mahazar and sketch, are contrary to the actual facts at the place of accident.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV Reports, wherein the damages caused to the vehicles are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect damages being caused to the offending vehicle.
The owner or rider of offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation related to the manner in which the vehicle got damaged.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex.P.7 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P8 is the notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given to said notice is marked as Ex.P.9.
In the notice issued by I O, it is mentioned about involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and about negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The owner of the offending vehicle has given reply to the notice as per Ex.P.9.

In the reply given to the notice, the owner of the offending vehicle does not appear to have denied the involvement of offending vehicle and also the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of the vehicle.
The owner of the offending vehicle has got the opportunity to deny the involvement of vehicle and the negligence of driver of the vehicle.
But, the recitals of reply notice do not disclose the aspect of denial of involvement of vehicle in the accident as well as negligence of rider of offending the vehicle in the cause of accident.
The said document also discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the owner of the offending vehicle for the Kumar A.R. Alias Kumarappa A.R vs Sujith Kumar Guptha on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162073866/

sentences.text: In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The rider or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioner could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
13. Further, on perusal of the materials, there appears to be delay of 24 days in lodging first information statement.
The accident occurred on 27.10.2022.
As per Ex.P.2, first information statement, petitioner himself has lodged a complaint with police on 19.11.2022.
As per the materials placed on record, there was 24 days delay in lodging complaint.
The petitioner in his complaint explained that he was in hospital and was taking treatment as an inpatient and thereafter lodged the complaint with the police.

Further, on perusal of hospital documents placed by the petitioner,
immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to the hospital.
In general parlance, the injured as well as his family members think about providing best treatment to the patient rather than to lodge complaint before the police.
Only on the ground of delay in lodging complaint the claim cannot be doubted and the case cannot be dismissed.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan in (2011) 4 SCC 693, held that delay in lodging a FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimants case.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this tribunal cannot dismiss the petition only on the ground of delay in lodging the complaint.
No materials are placed to create doubt about contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of respondent in the cause of accident.
Merely because there is delay in lodging the first information statement, the case of the petitioner cannot be considered to be doubtful.
14. On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.R.1 & 2.
The evidence of Rw-1 is not sufficient and satisfactory to disprove or rebut the contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Evidence of RW.1 is not of much assistance to the respondents to disprove or rebut the contentions of petitioner related to accident and negligence of rider of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA- 04-JW-4744 by its rider and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner has produced Wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, wherein it discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.
The petitioner not furnished discharge summary in order to know the nature of treatment availed by him and the period of treatment.
The petitioner examined Dr.S.Ramachandra as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P21 & 22.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent partial impairment of left lower limb at 17.2% and to the whole body at 8.6%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has produced 46 medical bills for a sum of .25,290/- marked at Ex.P.11 and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.12.
The bill furnished at serial No.2 does not appear to be pertaining to the petitioner.
The name of the patient is mentioned as Mohanamba in the said bill and it does not disclose the name of petitioner as a patient.
PW.1 also admitted in the cross examination that bill No.4 does not pertain to him.
As such, the petitioner is not entitled to the amount mentioned in serial No.4 of Ex.P.11 which is .230/-.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said documents.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also, nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .25,060/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges: On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 27.10.2022 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of materials on record, the petitioner appears to have taken treatment at the hospital for the injuries sustained by him.
So, during the time of treatment the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.
The petitioner has not produced discharge summary to show that he took treatment as an inpatient.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that Kumar A.R. Alias Kumarappa A.R vs Sujith Kumar Guptha on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162073866/

(iv) Towards Conveyance:
The petitioner is the resident of Gangondanahalli Main Road, Nalagadaranahalli,
Nagasandra Post, Bengaluru and he has admitted to hospital for availing treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has not produced discharge summary.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:

The petitioner contended that he was working as a Police Head Constable in Karnataka Police Department Bengaluru and getting salary for a sum of .57,000/-
per month.
The petitioner contended that, due to accident he was unable to attend his work regularly.

On perusal of record, the petitioner sustained left leg abrasions,
left knee tenderness, left knee ROM painful and restricted and as per X-ray left leg shows left proximal tibia fracture and severe injuries to hand and head and was treated conservatively.
The petitioner contended that due to accidental injuries he has not attended his work and he was on leave.
In order to prove his contention he has produced Ex.P.14 - Salary slips for the month of August 2022 to December 2022.
Further the petitioner has produced bank statement, which is marked at Ex.P.15.
The petitioner has also produced ID Card marked at Ex.P.17.

Ex.P.16 - Letter issued by Deputy Commissioner of Police, Bengaluru Urban, wherein he has stated that the petitioner by name Sri.Kumarappa.A.R, HC.No.9181, R.T.Nagar Police Station, who applied leave for medical reason and he took commuted leave from 28.10.2022 to 27.11.2022 i.e., for a period of 31 days, E.L from 28.11.2022 to 12.12.2022 i.e., for a period of 15 days, E.L. from 13.12.2022 to 13.02.2023 i.e., for a period of 63 and petitioner appears to be on leave for a total period of 109 days.
The petitioner not furnished any materials to show that during the period of leave he has not been paid salary.
The petitioner not examined the concerned officer of the department to show that he was not paid salary during the period of leave.
PW.1 stated in the cross examination that the salary there was no deduction in his salary during the period of treatment.
As per the materials on record, the petitioner is working as a police constable and is a Government servant.
Further, the materials on record do not disclose that the leave granted to the petitioner is without salary.
The petitioner not furnished materials to show that there was loss of income/salary to him during the period treatment.
As per the materials on record, the petitioner applied E.L and commuted leave on medical ground.
The leave applied by petitioner does not appear to be without salary.
The petitioner is a salaried person and there appears to be no dispute with respect to the said aspect.
The leave applied by petitioner does not appear to be without salary and the petitioner also not furnished any materials to show that he has not been paid salary during the period of leave.

The petitioner not Kumar A.R. Alias Kumarappa A.R vs Sujith Kumar Guptha on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162073866/
7 furnished satisfactory materials to show that he has loss of income during the period of treatment.

sentences.text: As such, the petitioner is not entitled for loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Permanent Disability:
The petitioner contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.S.Ramachandra working as Consultant in Orthopedic and DNB Post Graduates Professor at General Hospital, Jayanagar, Bengaluru as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.
The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained left proximal tibia fracture (left leg) and severe injuries to hand and head and was treated conservatively on outpatient basis.
The doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability to left lower limb to the extent of 17.2% and to the whole body at 8.6%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.21 & 22 i.e., OP Record with clinical notes and X-ray film.

The petitioner has contended that he was working as a Police Head Constable in Karnataka Police Department Bengaluru and getting salary for a sum of .57,000/-
per month.
Further the petitioner also not proved that due to accidental injuries, he has lost his income and he was not going for job.
In the cross-examination, PW.1 admitted that he is presently working in the same post and in the same department.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that there is loss of income to him due to accidental injuries.
The materials on record disclose that the petitioner is continuing his job and receiving the salary.
There appears to be no loss of income for the petitioner due to accidental injuries.
The petitioner is still working in the police department and drawing salary.
Further, the petitioner not furnished materials to show that the disability, as stated by doctor, causing problems in performing his duties and due to the same, there is loss of income to him.
The materials on record disclose that the petitioner is still working in the department in which he worked prior to the accident.
Further, there appears to be no reduction in the salary due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of loss of income to the petitioner due to the accidental injuries.
In ILR 2010 KAR 2439, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Kartakana it is held that if there is no loss of income, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.

"It has to be born in mind while awarding compensation of future loss of earnings,
there must be evidence to show that as a result of the injury, the income was reduced or there was loss of earnings or he was removed from service on account of disability or he is incapable of doing any work.
In the absence of these factors, the question of awarding compensation on heading loss of future earnings does not arise".
On perusal of cross-examination, PW.1 is working as Police constable and drawing the salary.
So there is no reduction of income due to accidental injuries and also he continued in the job.

Hence,
the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of permanent disability.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:-
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day- today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

17. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .1,00,060/- (Rupees One Lakh Sixty only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 3 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.
Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 27.10.2022 at about 08.50 p.m., to 09.00 p.m., on Dinnur Main Road at Citizen Park Back side road, Bengaluru, when petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KJ-8911, due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-JW-4744 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner has contended that on 27.10.2022 at about 08.50 to 09.00 p.m.,
accident occurred on Dinnur Main Road at Citizen Park Back Side Road, Bengaluru, when he was riding Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-KJ-8911, due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-JW-4744 by its rider in which he sustained grievous injuries.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the reply given to the notice, the owner of the offending vehicle does not appear to have denied the involvement of offending vehicle and also the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of the vehicle.
The owner of the offending vehicle has got the opportunity to deny the involvement of vehicle and the negligence of driver of the vehicle.
But, the recitals of reply notice do not disclose the aspect of denial of involvement of vehicle in the accident as well as negligence of rider of offending the vehicle in the cause of accident.
The said document also discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the owner of the offending vehicle for the Kumar A.R. Alias Kumarappa A.R vs Sujith Kumar Guptha on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162073866/
4 offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC as per Ex.P.10.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The rider or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.
In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Only on the ground of delay in lodging complaint the claim cannot be doubted and the case cannot be dismissed.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this tribunal cannot dismiss the petition only on the ground of delay in lodging the complaint.
No materials are placed to create doubt about contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of respondent in the cause of accident.
Merely because there is delay in lodging the first information statement, the case of the petitioner cannot be considered to be doubtful.
The evidence of Rw-1 is not sufficient and satisfactory to disprove or rebut the contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
The materials on record disclose that the petitioner is still working in the department in which he worked prior to the accident.
Further, there appears to be no reduction in the salary due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
In ILR 2000 KAR 3443 in between United India Insurance company Ltd., Vs. DC Rajan and another the Hon'ble High court held at para 6 as follows;
Kumar A.R. Alias Kumarappa A.R vs Sujith Kumar Guptha on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162073866/
8
On perusal of cross-examination, PW.1 is working as Police constable and drawing the salary.
So there is no reduction of income due to accidental injuries and also he continued in the job.
Hence,
the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of permanent disability.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:-
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.
opennyai_summary.decision:
17. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl
. No .
Particulars Amount  a. Towards injury pain and .50,000/-
 suffering  b. Towards Medical Expenses .25,060/-
 c. Towards food and extra .5,000/-
 nourishment and medical  attendant  d. Towards conveyance .10,000/-
 e. Deprivation of future .10,000/-
 amenities
Total compensation .1,00,060/-
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of .1,00,060/-.
18. In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
19. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
So, the respondent No.1 & 3, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .1,00,060/- (Rupees One Lakh Sixty only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 3 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
